title: Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering
seo_title: Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering | Dataq Software
meta_description: Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering services from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Dataq Software's Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering practice: what the tower covers, the services inside it, the platforms it deploys and the outcomes typical programs commit to.

Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering builds the runtime for everything else we do: hybrid and multicloud architecture, cloud-native modernization of legacy estates, edge and distributed infrastructure for latency-critical operations, SRE and reliability engineering, internal developer platforms, FinOps, and mission-critical high-performance systems. We measure ourselves on availability, lead time, and unit economics — not migration counts.

Lift-and-shift savings have evaporated; the value now sits in platform leverage. A strong internal platform cuts service onboarding from months to days, FinOps discipline turns cloud spend from a board escalation into a unit metric, and edge estate is mandatory for plants, ports, grids and stores where 200 milliseconds of latency is a lost order or a failed inspection.

items: The estate as designed system: landing zones, network fabric and workload placement by economics.

Compute where the physics is: edge estate for plants, stores, vehicles and grids.
Reliability as product: SLOs, error budgets and incident discipline that engineers actually follow.
Golden paths, paved roads: an internal platform that turns months into days.
Cost and carbon as engineering metrics: unit economics, showback and green compute by design.
When microseconds and uptime are the product: HPC, low-latency and always-on engineering.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.

A running record of the delta against baseline, updated at every gate, reviewed at every steering meeting.
